title: New Study: AI Ads Match Human Creative in Major Report from Columbia University, Harvard University, Technical University of Munich, and Carnegie Mellon University; Taboola Data Shows AI Wins by Appearing Authentically Human and Prioritizing Visual Trust Signals

body_text: NEW YORK, NY – Taboola (Nasdaq: TBLA), a global leader in delivering performance at scale for advertisers, today announced the findings of a major field study conducted in collaboration with researchers at Columbia University, Harvard University,Technical University of Munich, and Carnegie Mellon University. The research provides the first-ever look at how generative AI (GenAI) compares to human creativity in driving consumer action by analyzing large-scale real-world ad performance. While GenAI has revolutionized production speed and cost, its impact on actual performance has remained a subject of intense debate. The new study, titled, “ AI Ads That Work: How AI Creative Stacks Up Against Humans ,” analyzed hundreds of thousands of live ads running on Realize, Taboola’s performance advertising platform, totaling more than 500 million impressions and 3 million clicks. Key insights from the academic research include: GenAI ads perform just as well as human-made ads: AI-generated ads performed just as well as human-made ads. In raw data, AI ads saw a slightly higher average click-through-rate (CTR) (0.76%) compared to human ads (0.65%), though they performed comparably when researchers applied the tightest statistical controls. AI ads win the most when they don’t “look” like AI: AI-generated ads that did not “look like AI” achieved the highest engagement of all groups, significantly outperforming both human-made ads and AI ads that were perceived as artificial. Human faces are the “secret ingredient” for trust: The study found that one of the most important factors in making an ad feel “human” and trustworthy was the presence of a large, clear human face. Interestingly, based on Taboola’s best practices and policy restrictions, AI-generated ads were more likely to include these trust cues than their human-made counterparts. Brands no longer have to choose between speed and quality: AI-generated visuals increased or maintained click-through rates without reducing downstream conversion performance, proving that advertisers do not have to trade quality or conversions for production scale. Food, drink, and finance brands were among the first to adopt AI ads: Specific sectors; most notably, the “food and drink” and “personal finance” industries were early to adopt AI ads. “Taboola’s platform provided us with a literal gold mine of real-world data that is simply unavailable in a lab setting. By analyzing over 500 million impressions, we were able to move past the hype of GenAI and uncover its real impact in large scale settings,” said Oded Netzer, Vice Dean for Research, Columbia Business School. “Our findings prove that when AI is used to enhance human cues—like the trust found in a human face—it doesn’t just match human performance; it often sets a new ceiling for engagement.” Methodology The study utilized a quasi-experimental “sibling ads” approach, comparing matched pairs of AI-generated and human-made ads created by the same advertiser for the same campaign on the same day. This methodology allowed researchers to isolate the impact of the GenAI creative while controlling for external variables like the identity of the advertiser, timing, audience targeting, and landing pages. About Taboola Taboola empowers businesses to grow through performance advertising technology that goes beyond search and social and delivers measurable outcomes at scale. Taboola works with thousands of businesses who advertise directly on Realize, Taboola’s powerful ad platform, reaching approximately 600M daily active users across some of the best publishers in the world. Publishers like NBC News, Yahoo, and OEMs such as Samsung, Xiaomi and others use Taboola’s technology to grow audience and revenue, enabling Realize to offer unique data, specialized algorithms, and unmatched scale. title: Fresenius Medical Care accelerates the second tranche of its EUR 1 billion share buyback program with around EUR 415 million repurchase planned
body_text: Press Release The second tranche of the share buyback is expected to be executed by May 8, 2026 The share buyback program with a total volume of EUR 1 billion is expected to be completed in less than a year, significantly earlier than originally planned Bad Homburg (January 9, 2026) – Fresenius Medical Care (FME), the world’s leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal disease, will accelerate its share buyback program and start the repurchase of the second tranche. The program – presented during the company’s Capital Markets Day on June 17, 2025 – has a total volume of EUR 1 billion. Under the second tranche, the company plans to repurchase its own shares for a total amount of around EUR 415 million from January 12 to May 8, 2026. The first tranche of the company's share buyback program was completed ahead of schedule on December 29, 2025. The share buyback program, which is part of the FME capital allocation framework within the ‘FME Reignite’ strategy, is expected to be completed significantly earlier than originally planned, in less than a year. Helen Giza, CEO and Chair of the Management Board, said, “The successful acceleration of our EUR 1 billion share buyback program is supported by our strong financial performance and consistent execution against our ‘FME Reignite’ strategy, with a focus on value creation and delivering returns to our shareholders.” “Our strong cash-flow generation on the back of continued business momentum enables an acceleration of our share buyback program, demonstrating the effectiveness of our new capital allocation framework,” said Martin Fischer, CFO of Fresenius Medical Care. FME will provide regular updates on the progress of the share buyback program at https://freseniusmedicalcare.com/en/investors/shares/share-buy-back/ . About Fresenius Medical Care: Fresenius Medical Care is the world's leading provider of products and services for individuals with renal diseases of which around 4.2 million patients worldwide regularly undergo dialysis treatment. Through its network of 3,628 dialysis clinics, Fresenius Medical Care provides dialysis treatments for approximately. 294,000 patients around the globe. Fresenius Medical Care is also the leading provider of dialysis products such as dialysis machines and dialyzers. Fresenius Medical Care is listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (FME) and on the New York Stock Exchange (FMS). A humidity alarm at 3 a.m. shouldn't put your entire business at risk, but it does. One malfunctioning dehumidifier can compromise premium flower inventory before anyone unlocks the doors Tuesday morning. A security badge reader failure during a compliance audit can escalate into a licensing issue. A broken display case refrigeration unit can force you to pull products from the sales floor mid-shift. For dispensary operators, these breakdowns aren't simple maintenance headaches. They jeopardize your product, customer trust, brand reputation, and operating license. Your point of sale (POS) system handles transactions and loyalty programs, your digital menu drives purchasing decisions, and your seed-to-sale platform manages compliance tracking. But none of them notifies you when a climate control unit drifts outside acceptable parameters or when your last vault inspection wasn't documented. Cannabis retail demands a unified approach to facilities oversight. Facilities management software gives dispensaries and cannabis businesses the tools to schedule preventive maintenance (PM), monitor work orders in real time, coordinate contractors, safeguard inventory, and maintain documentation for state regulators. We evaluated nine facilities management software platforms through the lens of cannabis operations, facility requirements, and multi-state expansion. Here's what we found. How We Compare the Best Facilities Management Software for Cannabis Dispensaries Dispensaries operate under regulations that vary by state, license category, and municipal code. Facilities management software designed for a convenience store won't automatically address the needs of cannabis operations. Our evaluation centers on compliance capabilities and criteria that matter for cannabis retail, MSOs, and vertically integrated companies: Compliance documentation: Support for audit-ready logs covering security systems, vault equipment, refrigeration units, HVAC, and environmental controls Multi-location scalability: Ability to manage 5 locations or 50 while adapting to different state regulations and inspection protocols Vendor management: Tools that help track contractor access, record visit history, and simplify communication with HVAC, security, and facilities vendors Mobile functionality: User-friendly workflows for budtenders and store managers who need fast, in-store work request submission Integration potential: API support for enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, cannabis POS systems, customer relationship management (CRM) tools, e-commerce platforms, and delivery management systems Pricing transparency: Clear understanding of subscription costs, vendor fees, and add-on modules Best Facilities Management Software for Cannabis Dispensaries: Software Reviews Here's how the leading facilities management software platforms compare when assessed through the needs of cannabis dispensaries. 1. OpenWrench Best for: Multi-location MSOs wanting vendor cost transparency and hybrid maintenance teams OpenWrench distinguishes itself for cannabis businesses operating dispensaries across multiple states. The platform supports a hybrid model where you can coordinate internal maintenance staff and external vendors through a single dashboard. That structure proves valuable when you're managing refrigeration specialists in Nevada and alarm system technicians in Arizona. What makes OpenWrench compelling for cannabis operations is its approach to vendor costs. Unlike platforms that mark up contractor fees or charge transaction percentages, OpenWrench passes through vendor costs at face value. For dispensaries operating on tight margins, this can significantly affect profitability. MaintainX Best for: Dispensaries needing structured communication and audit-ready checklists MaintainX integrates real-time messaging into each work order, which helps cannabis operations eliminate communication gaps between stores, technicians, and managers. Its checklist builder supports daily security checks, HVAC inspections, and safety audits required for compliance. The platform's mobile-first design simplifies ongoing documentation for teams that need consistent proof of maintenance activity. Key features Work orders with integrated chat, inspection checklists, AI maintenance planner, asset management with document storage, internet of things (IoT) integration Pricing Basic: Free Essential: $20/user/month (annual) Premium: $65/user/month (annual) Enterprise: Quote-based Pros Clear messaging within every work order Strong inspection and compliance workflows Generous free tier Easy-to-use mobile interface Cons Free tier limits active work orders Multi-site analytics less robust than enterprise tools MaintainX suits cannabis teams wanting organized communication, reliable audit histories, and a mobile interface that teams can learn quickly. 4. Limble Best for: Growing dispensary chains wanting speed and pricing transparency Limble earns high marks for usability and rapid implementation. Its notifications keep teams informed on work orders, and its real-time dashboards help operators monitor equipment status and inventory levels across dispensaries. Inventory management features support cannabis teams wanting better visibility into parts usage. Transparent pricing and included support make it accessible for growing multi-location operations. Key features Work orders with notifications, PM automation, asset tracking, inventory management, mobile app, customizable dashboards Pricing Custom quotes. Limble does not publish plan pricing on its site. Pros High user satisfaction Predictable pricing Fast setup Strong support Cons Predictive maintenance sold separately Lighter IoT functionality Occasional bugs Limble gives dispensaries a balanced maintenance system that stays easy to use as the business expands. 5. Preventive maintenance relies on a calendar-based system that works well for HVAC, odor control, and refrigeration schedules. Optional modules, such as fleet management for delivery vehicles, extend the platform when needed. Customer support includes lifetime access and implementation that can take as little as two weeks. Key features Easy work request portal, calendar-based PM scheduling, fleet tracking, room scheduling, optional IT ticketing Pricing Quote-based Pros Very easy to use Strong customer support Fast rollout Cons Originally designed for schools and municipal buildings Analytics require an add-on Limited pricing transparency FMX is practical for cannabis dispensaries wanting a maintenance tool with minimal setup and a straightforward interface. 6. Its workflows streamline not-to-exceed (NTE) approvals, warranty checks, and vendor dispatching. Business intelligence tools help optimize facilities spend, benchmark vendor performance, and support clearer decision-making on repair-versus-replace choices. GPS check-in features help verify technician access to secure dispensary environments. These functions support cannabis retail teams that need dependable documentation during state inspections. Key features Automated work order workflows, asset management with repair-versus-replace recommendations, vendor marketplace, business intelligence dashboards, mobile apps with GPS tracking Pricing Not publicly listed. Vendors pay a commission on work routed through the marketplace. Pros Strong scalability for national brands Deep analytics for facilities spend Access to a large contractor network Cons Higher starting price Complex implementation Vendor fees may influence contractor pricing ServiceChannel works best for cannabis companies already operating at enterprise scale and ready to formalize maintenance across a large footprint. 9. Corrigo Best for: Large enterprise cannabis operations with automation needs Corrigo supports high-volume maintenance environments and processes billions in annual spend. Its automation reduces manual tasks, and its prescriptive analytics help teams choose vendors, optimize budgets, and manage asset life cycles. The mobile experience mirrors the desktop version, which helps large teams stay aligned. These features support cannabis businesses wanting structured, repeatable workflows across states. Key features Automated approvals, warranty checks, repair-versus-replace recommendations, vendor scoring, configurable reports, REST API Pricing Custom quote. Estimated starting costs fall within enterprise ranges. Pros Extensive automation for high-volume environments Prescriptive analytics that guide spend and vendor decisions Strong multi-location support Cons Higher cost compared to mid-market facilities management software Longer implementation timeline Complexity may exceed needs for smaller operators Corrigo suits cannabis operators with established facilities teams and the resources to maintain an enterprise system. Which Facilities Management Software is Right for Your Dispensary? The right platform depends on how your cannabis operations and broader business operations run and where you expect to grow. 5–50 locations: OpenWrench offers clear visibility across sites, real-time updates, and vendor cost transparency. It fits cannabis retail chains needing consistent maintenance without slowing store teams. Single-location dispensary: UpKeep, MaintainX, or Limble provide a user-friendly, cost-effective foundation for inventory management, issue reporting, and compliance workflows. Large MSOs: ServiceChannel and Corrigo deliver the automation and analytics required for complex cannabis operations across multiple states. Vertically integrated cannabis companies: Fiix supports retail storefronts and cultivation environments with predictive maintenance and seamless integration options. title: Product Updates: January 2026
summary: Suger January 2026: multi-partner collaboration on Azure referrals, a Salesforce dashboard for marketplace performance, and co-sell contact analytics.
body_text: What’s New in January 2026 This month, we focused on giving partnership and sales teams the visibility and collaboration tools they need to close complex deals faster. Here’s what’s now available on Suger. Introducing Multi-Partner Collaboration for Azure Referrals Close Azure deals faster by coordinating multiple partners in one unified workflow. Complex enterprise deals often require expertise from multiple partners—one for Azure infrastructure, another for implementation, and Microsoft for co-sell support. Until now, managing these multi-partner engagements meant juggling email threads, spreadsheets, and manual status updates. Partners worked in silos, and deal coordination could take days or weeks. What’s new: You can now invite multiple partners to collaborate on a single Azure referral directly within Partner Center. When you create a referral, the system generates individual copies for each invited partner while maintaining a centralized Microsoft Referral Set for visibility across all participants. How it works: Create your referral and invite partners from your network Each partner receives their own copy with specific deal details, team members, and solutions they’re contributing Partners can accept or decline invitations, and their status updates automatically You maintain full control: only you can invite additional partners (as long as the deal is active) Privacy is built-in: partner confidential information remains isolated unless they consent to share Key benefits: Reduce coordination time from days to minutes by bringing all partners into one system Never lose visibility into who’s contributing what to your Azure deals Maintain control while enabling true collaboration across your partner ecosystem Salesforce Dashboard for Marketplace Performance Stop pulling marketplace data from three different places. See your AWS, Azure, and GCP performance in one dashboard. Partnership and sales leaders consistently tell us the same story: “I have no idea how my marketplace business is actually performing.” Revenue is flowing through AWS, Azure, and GCP, but tracking adoption, conversion rates, and revenue trends means exporting data, building custom reports, and living in Excel hell. What’s new: Native Salesforce dashboards that visualize your marketplace performance across all three clouds—AWS, Azure, and GCP—using your existing Suger Offer and Suger Entitlement data. What you can now track: Sales & Growth: Accepted offers per month, average acceptance time, top customers by revenue Funnel Performance: Opportunities shared to cloud marketplaces, marketplace close rates, conversion metrics Transaction Insights: New vs. existing customers, contract vs. pay-as-you-go splits, resale vs. direct transactions Financial Health: Overdue payments, refund trends, public offer activity Geographic Distribution: Transaction volume by country Key benefits: Out-of-the-box insights: Dashboards work immediately once your data is synced—no custom development required Cross-cloud visibility: See performance across AWS, Azure, and GCP in one place Easily customizable: Clone and modify dashboards to match your specific reporting needs Co-sell Partner Contact Analytics See each contact’s track record and performance metrics before you engage. When co-selling with a partner sales rep, you need context fast. What’s their win rate? What size deals do they typically close? Are they currently active? Without this visibility, partnership decisions have been based on gut feel rather than data. What’s new: Comprehensive analytics for every partner contact across AWS, Azure, and GCP co-sell referrals. Now you can see individual contact performance, revenue attribution, and engagement history at a glance. What you can now see: View contact metrics directly from the co-sell referral detail page Quick validation panel shows snapshot metrics (active deals, YTD revenue, win rate) Drill into complete detail page for historical trends, deal breakdowns, and time-period analysis Filter by year and cloud partner type for deeper insights Key benefits: Make data-driven partnership decisions with full visibility into contact performance Prioritize high-value relationships with contacts who consistently deliver results If you’d like to see how these capabilities fit into your current GTM motion, we’d be happy to walk you through it.

title: Sonos Appoints Carmine Arabia, Mandy Fields and Joe Kennedy to Board of Directors
summary: The additions strengthen the Board with deep operating, financial, and technology platform expertise as Sonos enters its next phase of growth.
body_text: January 12 2026, 16:14 (EST) Sonos Appoints Carmine Arabia, Mandy Fields and Joe Kennedy to Board of Directors SANTA BARBARA, Calif., January 12, 2026 – Sonos, Inc. (Nasdaq: SONO) today announced the appointment of Carmine Arabia, Mandy Fields and Joe Kennedy to its Board of Directors. The additions strengthen the Board with deep operating, financial, and technology platform expertise as Sonos enters its next phase of growth. “These three leaders bring impressive and highly complementary experience, as Sonos focuses on delighting customers and building durable, long-term value for shareholders,” said Julius Genachowski, Chair of the Sonos Board of Directors. “Carmine has unmatched experience scaling complex global hardware platforms. Mandy adds rigorous financial leadership shaped by helping build a culturally resonant consumer brand. Joe contributes the perspective of a seasoned public company CEO who has grown and operated a category-defining technology business. Together they add depth across hardware, finance, and consumer technology as the Board supports Sonos’ long-term strategy and execution.” Carmine Arabia is Vice President of Devices at Meta, where he leads the teams responsible for bringing virtual reality and AI-powered devices to market at global scale. His experience spans product operations, engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and launch execution across one of the world’s most complex connected hardware portfolios. Prior to Meta, Arabia was Vice President, Product Operations for Amazon’s consumer electronics devices and Senior Vice President, Global Manufacturing and Supply Chain at Blackberry. Mandy Fields is Chief Financial Officer of e.l.f. Beauty, where she has served since 2019 and helped guide the company through a period of sustained growth, operational discipline, and brand expansion. She brings more than two decades of financial and operating experience, including prior CFO leadership at BevMo! and senior finance and analytics roles at Albertsons. Earlier in her career, she worked in investment banking, developing a strong foundation in capital markets and strategic finance. Joe Kennedy is a longtime consumer technology executive and former public company CEO. As a member of the team that created Pandora, he served as Chief Executive Officer and President from the birth of the service through its growth as a publicly traded company, helping define the modern streaming media category. Prior to Pandora, Kennedy was President and Chief Operating Officer of E-LOAN and previously held senior leadership roles at General Motors. The Board appointments come as Sonos sharpens its focus on executing a clear, platform-driven strategy centered on the Sonos System as its core advantage. With more than 17 million households and over 53 million connected devices, the company is aligning its hardware, software, and go-to-market efforts around deepening household engagement, increasing lifetime value, and bringing new homes into the ecosystem. The expanded Board adds relevant operating, financial, and platform experience to help guide Sonos as it delivers against these priorities in fiscal 2026 and beyond. About Sonos Sonos (Nasdaq: SONO) is a leading audio company dedicated to elevating life through sound. Since pioneering multi-room wireless audio in 2005, Sonos has built a connected system that brings together every dimension of sound, including music, movies, stories, and conversations. Its portfolio of home theater speakers, components, plug-in and portable speakers, and headphones grows more powerful with every room and device added. Trusted by more than 17 million households in over 60 countries, Sonos is headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. Learn more at www.sonos.com . title: Live Ventures’ Central Steel Fabricators Emerges as a Strategic Participant in the AI Data Center and Connectivity Infrastructure Cycle :: Live Ventures
body_text: Live Ventures’ Central Steel Fabricators Emerges as a Strategic Participant in the AI Data Center and Connectivity Infrastructure Cycle Download as PDF January 27, 2026 LAS VEGAS and BROADVIEW, Ill., Jan. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Central Steel Fabricators, a portfolio company of Live Ventures Incorporated (NASDAQ: LIVE), today highlighted its expanding role as a critical infrastructure provider to the rapidly accelerating artificial intelligence (AI), automation, and data-center ecosystem. With a manufacturing heritage spanning major technological transitions, Central Steel Fabricators has provided essential infrastructure for the advent of digital telecommunications, the internet, and modern mobile telecom networks. Central Steel Fabricators manufactures precision-fabricated steel systems used in data centers and the connectivity that links them to the world, including cable management systems, structural frames, and custom components. The company continues to scale automation and robotic welding to increase throughput and support rising demand. Robotic welding initiatives have materially increased daily production capacity, positioning Central Steel Fabricators to respond rapidly to large-scale AI infrastructure programs and fiber deployments. According to Live Ventures management, Central Steel Fabricators’ automation, capacity expansion, and exposure to AI-driven infrastructure investment position the company to benefit from long-term secular growth trends. Thomas R. Sedlak, head of Live Ventures’ steel companies and CEO of Central Steel Fabricators, affirmed the potential of AI-driven business for the company’s future. He said, “I believe the opportunities for companies like ours that focus on the unmet needs of data center contractors are limitless.” About Central Steel Fabricators Central Steel Fabricators is a U.S.-based manufacturer of precision-fabricated steel systems serving the telecommunications, data-center, and infrastructure markets. The company provides the majority of Engineer, Furnish, and Install contractors throughout the country who manage projects for major communications providers. The company provides product to all the major distributors, with some stocking product while others drop ship material from Central Steel Fabricators’ warehouse. AI-driven data center build-outs have become major users of the company’s comprehensive product line. About Live Ventures Live Ventures Incorporated (Nasdaq: LIVE) is a diversified holding company focused on acquiring and operating domestic middle-market companies with strong cash flows and durable market positions. Its portfolio companies incorporate AI, robotics, data-based analytics, and other advanced systems to transform conventional operations into more efficient, competitive enterprises for the revolutionary AI era.
